$comment: Notices and notifications echo the reactor (GLASS_HUD §10, §11; the brief's 'Chat platforms and notifications'). One table, read by every surface that shows a notice without a drawn reactor — the web's notifications panel and toast (aura-web/src/lib/glass/bodies/notices.ts), the phone's notifications (android-app CompanionNotifications and its kin), the desktop shell's native notifications, and the chat-platform templates (hermes/plugins/_shared/_messages.py). A level names the reactor state whose glyph it carries and the colour it is drawn in; the glyph characters themselves come from design/build.py's REACTOR_GLYPHS through the generated files (STATE_GLYPH, console-theme.json, _glyphs.py), never from here. `ok` is the one level with no reactor state — a reactor has no 'succeeded' — so it wears the steady ring in the semantic ok colour, and its word is the copy rule's ('Done, passed, approved').

aliases.$comment: The panel protocol's notice levels (docs/hermes-hud-protocol.md, hud-panels.json) and the toast bus's kinds as this table's.

templates.$comment: The notify.* templates every surface shares, with the level each carries. A surface renders the level's glyph, colour and word, then the template's own copy: sentence case, the action named on the button, an error saying what happened and what to do next.

notice.for: a plain notice (house_tell_user, send_notification, a brief's delivery)

recovered.for: a threshold back under its limit; telemetry back

alert.for: a threshold crossed; an error; a watchdog gone blind

approval.for: an approval or a clarifying question waiting on the person

refused.for: a call the approval matrix denied outright

goal.for: a goal set, continuing, parked or done — its own lifecycle glyphs are Hermes' (⊙ ↻ ⏳ ✓ ✗) and are pinned against hermes_cli.goals

stopped.for: a standing service that stopped and needs a tap to come back; a panic that needs clearing
